basics.name: James Swartwood
basics.title: Robotics Software Engineer II (CV/AI)
basics.about: Robotics and Computer Vision Engineer specializing in multi-agent LLM systems, human-in-the-loop interfaces, gesture control, and 3D perception.

bullets: Served as an individual contributor on multiple client projects.
Implemented a computer vision system for retail product monitoring.
Designed multi-agent LLM systems to parse unstructured input into fleet-wide commands and robot actions.
Engineered human-robot interfaces for human-in-the-loop robotics applications.
Developed ROS control packages for server farm automation.

media.title: Fresh Film - "Why we do what we do"
media.description: Showcase video representing engineering and development initiatives at Fresh Consulting.

bullets: Devised and led R&D projects, including user experience & safety, teaching methods, and human-robot interfaces such as vision and voice AI.
Represented the company for fundraising with multimillion-dollar parties, leading technical demos and occasionally traveling to meet with investors and clients.
Served as the point person in the Doosan Robotics partnership.

bullets: Designed a robotic arm gesture control system that was featured at TechCrunch Disrupt.
Featured in many promotional videos that pushed the company into the public spotlight.

experience.role: Research Assistant – Environmental Science & Computer Science
bullets: Applied computer vision to build environmental science research tools.
Developed image labeling software, saving researchers hundreds of manual hours.

media.title: Pole Detection & Classification Algorithm
media.description: This website describes the pole detection algorithm developed for hydrology research projects using snow data.

bullets: Developed a collision avoidance application that leveraged PCL in C++ to detect people and their trajectories in real time with a point cloud stream.
Implemented an algorithm to perform segmentation in real-time on a point cloud video stream using Euclidean clustering.
Designed, trained, and tested custom machine-learning models to detect additional objects.

media.title: Point Cloud People Detection Example
media.description: This screenshot was taken while performing real-time detection of people inside a point cloud representation.

bullets: Developed a ROS package to control an AMR and train waypoints.
Experienced simulating the system with Gazebo before running it on the live robot.
Developed XR executables within Unity for robot point-of-view applications.
Leveraged OpenCV and Azure Cognitive Services to trigger robot behaviors on object detection.
Organized and led self-defense seminars for a variety of groups: martial arts schools, college communities, and foster care support groups.
Developed a basic self-defense outline, published online, used as a starting point and discussion catalyst for anyone interested in learning how to better protect themselves and their communities.

media.title: Self Defense NW Website
media.description: Official portal outlining self-defense curricula and seminar schedules.

bullets: Fostering an inclusive environment built on mutual growth for students of all ages, identities, and backgrounds.
Created a grappling curriculum based on Japanese systems of martial arts that encourages self-defense practices and mobility over competition.
This grappling system has enabled folks of all ages and genders to comfortably participate in physical training with each other and grow together as martial artists.
Expanded student curriculum to include teaching assistant roles to nurture the next generation of instructors and provide practice caring for and training newer students of all ages.
Taught as an instructor in martial arts classes for all age groups, covering disciplines such as Song Moo Kwan Tae Kwon Do, Shotokan Karate, Judo, Wing Chun, and Arnis.
Developed junior curriculum to encourage children to engage more in their progression and have more leadership training opportunities at higher levels.
Instructed children's classes, ages 5 to 18, in various Japanese martial arts.

bullets: Facilitated another section of GEN ST 199, by serving as a teacher and a mentor for a class of students and helped support those students as they developed confidence in navigating the UW and Seattle.
